title: Helmwell Pharmacy integration: triage & ops scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
Quick working notes from intake + technical triage for Helmwell Pharmacy (medication triage assistant integrated into patient portal + pharmacist dashboard). Aim: capture requirements, known gotchas, rough implementation options and next steps for the SE/infra handoff.

Call snapshot (2025-02-06):
- Attendees: Marcus (Helmwell eng), Liam (product), Priya (Redwood SE), Jae (Redwood SE), Evelyn (security)
- Business need: reduce pharmacist triage time for refill/drug-interaction questions; surface reasons for denials and suggested next-steps. Must support PHI, audit logs, and 30-day retention by default with enterprise option.
- Target UX: chat in patient portal (low-latency, conversational), plus a pharmacist-facing summarization widget integrated into their PMS.

High-level requirements (customer stated):
- PHI must never leave their VPC; private deployment required (initial PoC on Redwood Private VPC).
- Support for FHIR queries to pull latest meds and allergies; read-only access for model runtime.
- Audit trail for every request/response, with token-level cost breakdown and redaction logs.
- Latency SLO for patient portal: P95 <= 600ms for short queries (single-turn); pharmacist dashboard can tolerate 1.5s.
- Availability target for production: 99.9% with on-call runbook.
- Redaction: proactively strip direct identifiers before logs leave customer control; support KMS/HSM integration.

Technical notes / constraints:
- Network: Helmwell will connect via VPC peering + site-to-site VPN for legacy PMS that cannot be VPC-native. Need to validate MTU and TCP window settings (they reported occasional TCP stalls on the VPN).
- Auth: OAuth2 service account for Redwood control plane + mTLS for runtime endpoints. Customer prefers per-environment KMS keys.
- Data flow: portal -> Redwood inference endpoint inside customer's VPC -> (optional) on-prem HL7/FHIR adapter to PMS. Must design for no egress to public internet for PHI.
- Model selection: suggested baseline = 13B instruction-tuned open model (quantized int8) for SLO/cost balance; fallback model (smaller) for burst or degraded GPU availability.
- KV/prefix cache: high reuse for templated refill prompts; enable prefix caching to meet latency SLO. Need to evaluate cache warmup strategy for new patients.
- Batching: patient portal traffic is spiky; configure dynamic batching with strict latency cap (max batch window 20ms for patient flows). For pharmacist bulk summarization jobs, use larger batch windows to reduce cost.
- Function calling: use for structured actions (create refill request, triage ticket, escalate to pharmacist). Ensure calls are idempotent and include request ids.
- Embeddings: plan to use local embeddings index (hosted in their VPC) for knowledge retrieval (policy docs, drug monographs). Must avoid sending embeddings to Redwood-hosted services.

Gotchas encountered / flagged by customer:
- PMS auth uses legacy cert rotation, requires a connector that can handle nonstandard TLS ciphers.
- Their HL7 adapter occasionally returns duplicate MedicationStatement records — need dedupe heuristics before handing to model.
- Some workflows require real-time stock checks (millisecond-level). Those should be handled by synchronous API calls from portal, not by LLM. Mark as out-of-band.
- PHI redaction edge case: documented allergy synonyms (e.g., nicknames for meds) can leak context; must include a domain-specific redaction/normalization step before logging.

Security / compliance notes:
- Must support customer KMS + optional HSM for signing audit records.
- Retention: default 30 days, retained in their storage; longer retention requires explicit opt-in and legal sign-off.
- Eval data: any evaluation prompts that include PHI must be scrubbed and run on a dedicated test dataset in their VPC.
- Pen test: customer expects a pen test window for Private control plane and runtime before production onboarding.

Implementation sketch (PoC -> Prod):
1) PoC (2–4 weeks): deploy Redwood Private in Helmwell dev VPC, stand up inference endpoint with 13B int8 model, configure FHIR read-only connector, basic function-calls (create-refill), short retention, smoke test with synthetic PHI.
2) Pilot (6–8 weeks): expand to staging, plug into pharmacist dashboard for summarization, enable KV caching, run latency load test (simulate portal traffic pattern), run security review and pen test.
3) Prod: reserved dedicated capacity (Redwood Dedicated) or customer-dedicated nodes; SLA / monitoring; runbook, on-call rotation, longer retention/backups.

Open technical questions (need answers before architecture final):
- Exact FHIR subset we can call for real-time triage (MedicationRequest, MedicationStatement, AllergyIntolerance?) — Marcus to send a sample export.
- Which PMS endpoints require VPN-only access vs. can be proxied through secure API gateway.
- Expected QPS peak from patient portal (they said ~12qps peak per region, confirm).
- Are there any vendor constraints on TLS ciphers / cert formats for connector?

Action items / next steps:
- Marcus: share sample FHIR payload and VPN topology (due 2025-02-13).
- Jae: spin up PoC infra template (dev VPC) and share Terraform snippet for KMS + VPC routing (due 2025-02-18).
- Evelyn: draft minimal compliance checklist for PHI redaction + pen test scope (due 2025-02-20).
- Priya: prepare prompt/eval set (synthetic PHI) for initial quality baseline + a checklist for caching warmup scenarios (due 2025-02-17).
- Schedule: next sync tentative 2025-02-21 10:00 PT (30m) to review PoC plan.

Prototype prompts / examples (for eval):
- "Patient: I'm out of metformin, can I get a refill?" -> expected: verify last refill date, check active prescriber, confirm no contradictions, propose "create refill request" function call + short pharmacist note.
- "Pharmacist widget: Summarize medication changes in last 90 days for Mr. X" -> expected structured bulleted summary with timestamps and prescriber ids (if available).

Risk matrix (quick):
- Data leakage to public endpoints: HIGH (mitigated by private deploy + KMS)
- Latency misses causing UX regressions: MED (mitigated by prefix caching + smaller time window batching)
- Model hallucination on medical facts: MED-HIGH (mitigated by RAG with vetted monographs + system-level guardrails; include deterministic references in responses)

Notes to self: keep early evals conservative — prefer higher-precision smaller answers over creative summaries. Prioritize traceability of decisions (why model suggested a refill) in the pharmacist UI.

If Marcus sends sample FHIR by EOD Friday, we can wire a minimal read-only adapter and run first end-to-end with synthetic tokens next week.

-- Priya
(working draft - will tidy for handoff once PoC infra snippets exist)
